Excuse me. Where is the subway, please?
Which subway? Where do you want to go?
To Central Park. My wife and I are tourists.
Oh, you don't need the subway. Central Park is close. Go straight ahead for four blocks.
Four blocks. Okay. And then?
Then turn left on 59th Street. The park is across from the big hotel.
Sorry, can you say that again, slowly?
Sure. Straight four blocks, turn left, and the park is on the corner.
Thank you very much!
How do I get to Central Park?
Can you say that again, slowly?
Go straight and turn left.
It is next to the bank.

Good morning. The museum is not far. Walk out of the hotel and turn left. Go straight for three blocks. At the corner with the bank, turn right. That is 53rd Street. Walk one more block. The museum is on your left, next to a small coffee shop. It is across from a big bookstore. It is about ten minutes on foot. You don't need a taxi.

Manhattan is easy, I promise. Streets go from east to west, and they have numbers: 42nd Street, 57th Street. Avenues go from north to south: Fifth Avenue, Sixth Avenue. A short block, from one street to the next, is about one minute on foot. A long block, between two avenues, is about three minutes. And the subway? There is a station on the corner of many streets. It is fast. Don't take a taxi at five o'clock!

Carlos and his wife are lost in Manhattan. Carlos says: Excuse me, where is the subway? A woman says: Go straight for four blocks. Then she says: Turn left on 59th Street. Carlos asks her to say it again, slowly. They find the park, across from the station.
